question: What is the idle timeout duration after which the embed sidecar exits to free approximately 150MB RSS when no `/embed` requests are received?
gold: lib/embed-server.js is a detached MiniLM sidecar (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dims) that OUTLIVES daemon restarts. It exits on HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT=2min with no /ping (daemon died without clean shutdown) OR IDLE_MS=30min with no /embed (frees ~150MB RSS). On daemon restart embed.js reconnects to the running sidecar — no model re-load.
title: Embed sidecar self-terminates: 2min no-heartbeat, 30min idle; MiniLM-L6-v2/384d

question: What value of `opts.origin` is used to isolate the threshold-gated population in `keepRateByBand`, and what `origin` type made up the entire sub-0.40 KEEP band in live data?
gold: keepRateByBand takes opts.origin to isolate the threshold-gated population. Live data showed the sub-0.40 KEEP band was ENTIRELY hand-asserted note->task edges (origin:'asserted'), never the lexical autowire path the threshold actually gates — folding them together corrupts the tuning curve. Rows missing `origin` (pre-stamping journals) match nothing when a filter is given.
ON_predicted: origin:'asserted'; the entire sub-0.40 KEEP band was hand-asserted note→task edges (origin:'asserted').
title: Sub-0.40 KEEP band is all hand-asserted edges, not the autowire path the threshold gates

question: What git merge strategy does `.gitattributes` assign to `.graph/**`, and what class of conflicts does it prevent when merging attempt-branch worktrees?
gold: .gitattributes assigns `.graph/** merge=ours` (overriding the older per-file `merge=union` — last matching line wins) because attempt-branch worktrees would otherwise cause delete/modify + checkpoint.json conflicts; the daemon is source of truth so the current branch's .graph wins wholesale, never content-merged. Merge drivers aren't portable, so each clone must run once: `git config merge.ours.driver true`.
ON_predicted: `.graph/** merge=ours` — the current branch's `.graph` wins wholesale, preventing delete/modify and checkpoint.json conflicts.
OFF_predicted:
I don't know.

The repository has no `.gitattributes` file (this isn't even a git repository), so I can't verify any such assignment.
title: .graph/** uses merge=ours and needs a one-time per-clone git config

question: What was the cost multiplier observed when injecting a forced full payload of approximately 25k characters compared to the ON/OFF baseline?
gold: Forced full payload (~25k chars) cost 1.63x ON/OFF; lean payload (~1-3k chars) cost 1.03x. The whole cost difference is cache_read on the injected payload - output tokens (real work) never moved. Lean injection is cost-neutral. Measure work with output_tokens; headline on cost-weighted gross (cache_read bills ~0.1x).
title: Injection cost = payload size only; the entire ON/OFF gap is cache_read, work never moved

question: What specific method did the cold agent use to solve all 3 wincase-c test cases despite a strategy-silent prose spec?
gold: wincase-c's rigging guard did NOT hold - cold solved 3/3 by reading the committed acceptance test, whose generator exposes expected behavior, no matter how strategy-silent the prose spec is. A fully-specified committed test (or dependency source, see silent-cap) for a pure function leaves no empirical gap. This is structural, not a spec-writing flaw - production is naturally held-out, the bench had to be re-engineered to look like it.
ON_predicted: Reverse-engineering the strategy from the committed acceptance test (whose generator exposed the expected behavior).
title: The oracle leak: an in-worktree test/dependency IS the answer key, so the agent reverse-engineers it

question: What specific problem occurs when the same hook events are wired in both `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json`?
gold: When merging adapters/cursor/settings.sample.json into .claude/settings.json, do not additionally wire the same events in .cursor/hooks.json - both fire and the gate/mint hooks run twice. The CLI even emits a warning for the native-.cursor/hooks.json path.

OFF_predicted: Hooks fire twice (duplicate execution) for each event.
title: Cursor: do NOT also wire the same hook events in .cursor/hooks.json - double execution

question: What command must each developer run once in their clone to activate the custom merge driver that prevents `.graph/**` conflicts?
gold: The daemon is the source of truth for graph state, so .gitattributes assigns '.graph/** merge=ours' - on any merge the current branch's .graph wins wholesale, never content-merged (avoids delete/modify + checkpoint.json conflicts from attempt-branch worktrees). Merge drivers aren't portable, so each fresh clone needs the one-time 'git config merge.ours.driver true' or merges break.
title: .graph/** is merge=ours; every clone must run 'git config merge.ours.driver true' once

question: What specific attribution mechanism caused ON's cache_read tokens to be incorrectly bucketed as 'plumbing', making it appear to use 65% less work?
gold: Early reporting used net tokens and saw ON look like 0.35x ('65% less work') - but attributionMcpServer tagging is sticky across post-call messages, bucketing most of ON's cache_read into 'plumbing'. Pure artifact, retracted. Use output_tokens (or fresh input+output) as the work measure, not net.
ON_predicted: attributionMcpServer tagging being sticky across post-call messages.
title: The net = gross - plumbing token metric was a retracted artifact of sticky MCP attribution
